methodology: Each utterance annotated as is_claim=true/false. For claims: expected extraction content provided. Used for precision/recall/F1 evaluation of LLM claim extractors.

utterances.text: The 90% startup failure rate is unchanged from pre-Lean Startup eras.
utterances.expected: Startup failure rate (~90%) unchanged by Lean Startup methodology

utterances.text: The framework hasn't moved the needle on outcomes — it only reduces the cost of failure.
utterances.expected: Lean Startup reduces failure cost, not failure occurrence

utterances.text: No single universally-agreed framework exists.
utterances.expected: No single universally-agreed startup strategy framework exists

utterances.text: title: "Canonical Lens — Startup Strategy"
| Structure | Business Model Canvas / Lean Canvas | Map the business model visually | HIGH |
The single most structural change in startup economics is cost inversion — building is now cheap but inference is expensive.
utterances.expected: Cost inversion is the most structural change: building cheap, inference expensive

utterances.text: SaaS margins dropped from mid-80s to 70s or lower by adding AI.
utterances.expected: SaaS margins dropped from 80%+ to ≤70% due to AI integration

utterances.text: > **Method:** 8 web_search queries across 5 dimensions
Lean Startup's vocabulary has achieved near-universal penetration but its full methodology is rarely practiced.
utterances.expected: Lean Startup vocabulary widely adopted but full methodology rarely followed

utterances.text: Founders avoid framework fatigue by never running more than one at a time.
utterances.expected: Founders use max one framework at a time to avoid fatigue

utterances.text: This is directly counter to textbook prescriptions.
utterances.expected: Practitioner behavior contradicts textbook recommendations

utterances.text: Graham's essay argues the conventional Silicon Valley wisdom — hire professional managers once you scale — is wrong.
utterances.expected: Paul Graham argues against hiring professional managers at scale (Founder Mode)

utterances.text: The best counterexamples (Jobs' return to Apple, Chesky's turnaround) suggest the mode is situational.
utterances.expected: Founder vs Manager mode is situational, not a progression (Jobs, Chesky examples)

utterances.text: See also: "Founder Mode Is a Dangerous Red Herring" counter-essays.
Porter published How Competitive Forces Shape Strategy in HBR in 1979.
Blank's core mantra: you cannot discover customers from your desk.
utterances.expected: Customer discovery requires leaving the office (Steve Blank)

utterances.text: The 2022-2023 correction exposed the cost: blitzscaled companies that never found unit economics collapsed.
utterances.expected: 2022-2023 market correction revealed blitzscaling failures lacked unit economics

utterances.text: D5 (Funding) determines D6 (Team) which determines D7 (Execution).
utterances.expected: Funding constrains team which constrains execution speed (causal chain)

utterances.text: Each is a node in the causal graph below.
Beyond a certain team size (~10-15 for software startups), adding people reduces per-person output.
utterances.expected: Team productivity per person decreases above 10-15 people in software startups

utterances.text: PMF is the single binary gate. All else is noise.
utterances.expected: Product-Market Fit is the only binary success gate

utterances.text: How is Success Defined in Startup Strategy?
Y Combinator and a16z dominate the definitional landscape for startup success.
utterances.expected: YC and a16z are the dominant authorities defining startup success

utterances.text: 42% of startups still fail from no market need — the exact problem Lean claims to solve.
utterances.expected: 42% of startups fail from no market need despite Lean Startup methodology

utterances.text: SWOT is pure subjectivity with no falsifiability — any founder can fill it to say what they already believe.
utterances.expected: SWOT analysis is unfalsifiable and merely reflects founder bias

utterances.text: Use the Canvas to design, Lean Startup to test, Disciplined Entrepreneurship to scale.
utterances.expected: Recommended framework sequence: BMC → Lean Startup → Disciplined Entrepreneurship

utterances.text: Revenue-per-employee is now the primary metric, not headcount.
utterances.expected: Revenue-per-employee replaced headcount as primary startup metric

utterances.text: The data consistently shows that in the vast majority of markets, there is no first-mover advantage.
utterances.expected: First-mover advantage is a myth in most markets (data-supported)

utterances.text: On Indie Hackers, the Lean Startup book is called terrible and outdated.
utterances.expected: Lean Startup book considered outdated by practitioner community (Indie Hackers)

utterances.text: Waterfall → Agile → Lean Startup → Blitzscaling → AI-native is the progression.
utterances.expected: Startup methodology evolved: Waterfall → Agile → Lean Startup → Blitzscaling → AI-native
